record.tranche_reason: It varies model depth allocations at fixed target sizes and measures validation perplexity, testing the effect of architecture shape with a different setup from the original scaling-law studies.
record.gate_note: The paper does not fit or test power laws, extrapolate losses, or find compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Its relevant results are the 200M depth-split ablation and junction/design ablations, which measure validation perplexity. Other reported benchmark, speculative-decoding, and resource results do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (nested Matryoshka suites), the paper sweeps ten depth splits at fixed sub-model parameter targets (50M/100M/200M, 20B tokens) and reports validation PPL gaps. This bears on V4, that shape matters little at fixed size. No power-law, extrapolation, compute-optimal or downstream-scaling analysis is done.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The main conclusion is that a nested Matryoshka 3B suite reaches near-parity with independently trained baselines on benchmarks and validation/OOD PPL, using 36% less training compute and speeding up speculative decoding by 14–26%. Ablations show junction norm-rescaling, fresh embeddings and distillation matter for smaller sub-models, and several depth splits give comparable PPL with lower KV cache. Appendix C cites Kaplan et al. that scale matters more than shape, as background.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains nested model suites and compares architecture shapes and junction/loss variants; it does not reproduce the original scaling-law experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Validation PPL changes with junction design and distillation configuration; the tested depth allocation also changes the resource/performance trade-off.

fits_no_version.finding: Matryoshka nested 500M/1.5B/3B sub-models match independently trained models' validation PPL at every checkpoint, using 36% less training compute.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nested jointly-trained sub-models can reach validation-loss parity with independently trained models of matched size.

fits_no_version.finding: In nested suites, junction design and integrated distillation change sub-model PPL (zero junction +0.54 avg PPL over the full recipe; removing distillation +0.15).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nesting-specific junction and distillation choices, not just size, set sub-model loss in nested suites.

record.problems: The depth-shape sweep is limited to the 200M proxy suite and is described partly qualitatively; individual values are plotted rather than tabulated. Junction and distillation variants do not isolate architecture shape alone.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were left out.

untested.parts: No power-law fit of loss vs parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.

Only ten depth splits at the 200M proxy scale (100M/200M block depths of 3–8 layers) are tested. Wider shape ranges, width/head/FFN-ratio variation and larger scales are not; the 3B depth sweep reports only KV cache and FLOPs, not loss.
Benchmarks are reported but not related to scale or loss.
No exponents or fitting choices are compared.

missing.what: Per-variant PPL or NLL gaps for the ten depth splits (only plotted) and the 1D PPL vs KV-cache summary showing average PPL about 20.0–20.4 across shapes
Authors' statement that matching the KV-cache footprint (depth-linked) matters for matching Vanilla performance, a possible qualifier on shape-insensitivity

record.verdict_notes: The V4 evidence is thin: it is a small qualitative depth sweep inside a novel nested architecture, with each variant compared to Vanilla rather than to the other shapes. The junction/recipe rows were moved off V4 because they vary method components at fixed shape, so the reader's limits_scope label is dropped.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fits for loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; the reported sizes and token budgets do not test the claimed power-law form over several orders of magnitude.
No prediction of larger-run losses from fits on smaller runs.
No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation sweep or growth-law fit.
Tests a limited set of depth allocations at the 200M proxy-suite scale and some junction/design variants; it does not test a wide range of architectures or larger scales.
Only text pretraining is studied; no other modalities, repeated-data regime, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling law is tested.
Downstream benchmarks are reported, but the study does not test whether downstream performance is predictably related to scale or pretraining loss.
No scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal splits are fitted or compared across fitting choices.

rows.subject: Matryoshka 200M proxy suite
rows.operation_detail: Swept ten depth-split variants, changing the depth allocation between the 100M and 200M blocks while keeping target sizes fixed.

conditions.value: ten variants; shared 50M base; 100M and 200M block depths varied

rows.measure: Mean validation perplexity gap versus the Vanilla baseline, averaged over the three sub-model sizes
rows.value: Several variants were comparable to Vanilla; the chosen (L1, L2) = (5, 4) configuration was described as having very low average PPL cost, and other variants reduced KV cache with comparable PPL.
rows.note: The paper describes the outcome qualitatively; the figure plots the individual variants. This supports small loss changes for the tested depth configurations, not across a broad architecture range.
rows.check: Value is qualitative. Fig 7b colorbar spans about ±0.4 mean PPL gap on PPL near 20, and Fig 14c shows average PPL about 20.0–20.4 across variants, i.e. roughly 2% spread. The comparison is each shape vs Vanilla, not shape vs shape, but the variants differ only in depth split.

relationships.condition: Ten depth-split variants of a 50M/100M/200M Matryoshka suite at fixed sub-model sizes, 20B tokens
relationships.reason: r1: the authors call several variants comparable to Vanilla in PPL. Plotted mean PPL gaps span about ±0.4 on PPL near 20 (Fig 7b, 14c), a small shape effect.
relationships.display_finding: Mean perplexity gaps were approximately ±0.4 around perplexity 20, with several variants comparable to Vanilla.
